topic: Broker Supervision, Principal Brokers & Management-Level Licensees
question: Under ORC 4735.081(A), what happens to an affiliated broker at a brokerage who is NOT designated as the brokerage's principal broker?
choice_a: That broker is either an associate broker or a management level licensee, depending on whether the broker has assigned supervisory duties
choice_b: That broker's license is automatically suspended until a redesignation occurs
choice_c: That broker must immediately surrender the license to the superintendent
choice_d: That broker automatically becomes principal broker of the brokerage's first branch office
explanation: ORC 4735.081(A) requires every brokerage to designate at least one affiliated broker as principal broker; any affiliated broker not so designated is, by the statute's own terms, an associate broker or a management level licensee -- not an unlicensed or suspended status.

topic: Broker Supervision, Principal Brokers & Management-Level Licensees
question: How does ORC 4735.01(AA) define an "associate broker"?
choice_a: An individual licensed as a real estate broker who does not function as the principal broker or a management level licensee
choice_b: A broker with fewer than 20 closed transactions in the preceding 5 years
choice_c: A broker who works exclusively under the direct supervision of a licensed salesperson
choice_d: A broker who holds a branch-office license but not a main-office license
explanation: ORC 4735.01(AA) defines "associate broker" by exclusion: an individual licensed as a real estate broker who is neither the principal broker nor a management level licensee at that brokerage.

topic: Broker Supervision, Principal Brokers & Management-Level Licensees
question: Broker Dana is licensed and affiliated with XYZ Realty, is not designated as principal broker, and has not been assigned any supervisory responsibility over other affiliated licensees. Under Ohio's statutory taxonomy, what is Dana's status?
choice_a: Dana is an associate broker
choice_b: Dana automatically qualifies as a management level licensee regardless of assigned duties
choice_c: Dana's license is deficient because Ohio law requires every broker to supervise at least one other licensee
choice_d: Dana must be redesignated principal broker within 15 days or lose licensure
explanation: Without a principal-broker designation or assigned supervisory duties meeting the management-level-licensee test, Dana falls into the residual category ORC 4735.01(AA) defines as associate broker.

topic: Broker Supervision, Principal Brokers & Management-Level Licensees
question: ORC 4735.01(FF) defines "management level licensee" using which general term, rather than restricting the role to holders of a broker's license specifically?
choice_a: "Licensee" -- broadly, a person employed by or affiliated with a real estate broker who has supervisory responsibility over other affiliated licensees
choice_b: "Broker" exclusively
choice_c: "Employee" exclusively
choice_d: "Officer" exclusively
explanation: ORC 4735.01(FF) defines management level licensee as "a licensee ... who has supervisory responsibility over other licensees," using the chapter's general licensee terminology rather than expressly limiting the role to broker's-license holders.

topic: Broker Supervision, Principal Brokers & Management-Level Licensees
question: Apart from the specific duties enumerated in ORC 4735.081(C), how does ORC 4735.01(HH) itself define "principal broker"?
choice_a: An individual licensed as a real estate broker who oversees and directs the operations of the brokerage
choice_b: An individual who has passed a separate principal-broker licensing examination
choice_c: An individual designated by the Ohio Real Estate Commission rather than by the brokerage itself
choice_d: An individual who owns at least 51 percent of the brokerage's equity
explanation: ORC 4735.01(HH) supplies the chapter's definitional shorthand for principal broker -- an individual licensed as a real estate broker who oversees and directs the operations of the brokerage -- which ORC 4735.081(C) then elaborates into fourteen specific enumerated duties.

topic: Broker Supervision, Principal Brokers & Management-Level Licensees
question: The definition of "principal broker" in ORC 4735.01(HH) ("oversees and directs the operations of the brokerage") most closely echoes which specific duty enumerated in ORC 4735.081(C)?
choice_a: C(1) -- "oversee and direct the operations of the brokerage"
choice_b: C(3) -- displaying the fair housing statement
choice_c: C(9) -- developing a written agency-relationship policy
choice_d: C(13) -- overseeing advertising compliance
explanation: ORC 4735.081(C)(1) restates, as the first enumerated duty, the same "oversee and direct the operations of the brokerage" language ORC 4735.01(HH) uses to define principal broker in the first place.

topic: Broker Supervision, Principal Brokers & Management-Level Licensees
question: ORC 4735.01(FF) defines "management level licensee" in general terms as a licensee with supervisory responsibility over other affiliated licensees. How does OAC 1301:5-6-01(A) narrow that statutory definition?
choice_a: By adding two conjunctive conditions: assigned oversight of a main office, branch office, or division, AND supervision of licensees whose agency duties to clients may conflict with other affiliated licensees
choice_b: By limiting the term to brokers with at least 10 years of licensed experience
choice_c: By requiring superintendent pre-approval before any management-level-licensee designation takes effect
choice_d: By extending the definition to also cover unlicensed office administrators
explanation: OAC 1301:5-6-01(A) operationalizes ORC 4735.01(FF)'s broad statutory definition into a specific two-part conjunctive test tied to assigned office/branch/division oversight and conflicting-agency-duty supervision.

topic: Broker Supervision, Principal Brokers & Management-Level Licensees
question: Under OAC 1301:5-6-01(A)(1), assigned oversight responsibility for which three organizational units of a brokerage can support management-level-licensee status?
choice_a: The brokerage's main office, a branch office, or a division
choice_b: Only the main office
choice_c: Branch offices only, not divisions
choice_d: Only divisions with five or more affiliated licensees
explanation: OAC 1301:5-6-01(A)(1) lists the main office, a branch office, or a division as the three organizational units whose assigned oversight can satisfy the first prong of the management-level-licensee test.

topic: Broker Supervision, Principal Brokers & Management-Level Licensees
question: Under OAC 1301:5-6-01(B), what does the rule say "supervisory activities" consist of?
choice_a: The general oversight of, or the direction of, activities conducted by other real estate licensees affiliated with the brokerage
choice_b: Exclusively the review and co-signing of every purchase contract the brokerage enters into
choice_c: Exclusively conducting affiliated licensees' annual performance reviews
choice_d: Exclusively approving marketing budgets for affiliated licensees
explanation: OAC 1301:5-6-01(B) defines supervisory activities broadly as general oversight or direction of the activities of other affiliated real estate licensees, not a narrow list of administrative tasks.

topic: Broker Supervision, Principal Brokers & Management-Level Licensees
question: Under ORC 4735.081(B), within how many days after a change in principal broker designation must a brokerage report the change to the superintendent?
choice_a: 15 days
choice_b: 5 days
choice_c: 30 days
choice_d: 45 days
explanation: ORC 4735.081(B) requires a brokerage to report any change in its principal-broker designation to the superintendent not later than fifteen days after the change occurs.

topic: Broker Supervision, Principal Brokers & Management-Level Licensees
question: Under ORC 4735.081(B), to whom must a brokerage report a change in its principal broker designation?
choice_a: The superintendent (of the Ohio Division of Real Estate)
choice_b: The county recorder in the county where the brokerage is located
choice_c: The Ohio Real Estate Commission's outside legal counsel exclusively
choice_d: The brokerage's errors-and-omissions insurance carrier
explanation: ORC 4735.081(B) directs the report of a principal-broker-designation change to the superintendent, the same official responsible for administering broker and salesperson licensure under Chapter 4735.

topic: Broker Supervision, Principal Brokers & Management-Level Licensees
question: On March 1, ABC Realty's principal broker resigns and the brokerage designates a new principal broker that same day. Under ORC 4735.081(B), by what date must ABC Realty report this change to the superintendent?
choice_a: No later than March 16 -- 15 days after the change occurred
choice_b: No later than March 31 -- 30 days after the change occurred
choice_c: The same day, March 1
choice_d: No report is required because the new designee already holds a broker's license
explanation: ORC 4735.081(B)'s 15-day clock runs from the date the designation change occurs, so a change occurring March 1 must be reported no later than March 16.

topic: Broker Supervision, Principal Brokers & Management-Level Licensees
question: Is reporting a change in principal broker designation to the superintendent optional under ORC 4735.081(B) if the outgoing and incoming principal brokers privately agree on the transition?
choice_a: No -- ORC 4735.081(B) requires the brokerage to report the change no later than 15 days after it occurs, regardless of any private agreement between the brokers
choice_b: Yes -- a private agreement between the two brokers satisfies the statute without a report to the superintendent
choice_c: Yes -- only publicly traded brokerages must report designation changes
choice_d: Yes -- reporting is required only if the incoming principal broker is newly licensed
explanation: ORC 4735.081(B) imposes an unconditional 15-day reporting obligation on the brokerage; nothing in the statute allows a private arrangement between brokers to substitute for that report to the superintendent.

topic: Broker Supervision, Principal Brokers & Management-Level Licensees
question: Under ORC 4735.081(C)(2), a principal broker must comply with office requirements found in which two other Chapter 4735 provisions?
choice_a: Division (A) of ORC 4735.13 and division (A) of ORC 4735.16
explanation: ORC 4735.081(C)(2) requires the principal broker to comply with the office requirements set forth in division (A) of section 4735.13 and division (A) of section 4735.16 -- distinct from the licensure-qualification provisions in 4735.07-.08.

topic: Broker Supervision, Principal Brokers & Management-Level Licensees
question: ORC 4735.081(C)(2)'s cross-reference to ORC 4735.13(A) most directly ties the principal broker's duty to which underlying requirement?
choice_a: Maintaining a definite place of business and properly licensing/displaying the brokerage's office(s)
choice_b: Filing the brokerage's annual state tax return
choice_c: Registering the brokerage's trademark with the secretary of state
choice_d: Maintaining a minimum brokerage net-worth threshold
explanation: ORC 4735.13(A) is the definite-place-of-business and office-licensing provision of Chapter 4735; ORC 4735.081(C)(2) folds compliance with that requirement into the principal broker's statutory duty list.

topic: Broker Supervision, Principal Brokers & Management-Level Licensees
question: How does ORC 4735.081(C)(2)'s office-requirements duty differ from the advertising-compliance-oversight duty listed separately at ORC 4735.081(C)(13)?
choice_a: C(2) requires compliance with the definite-place-of-business rule of 4735.13(A) and the advertising-disclosure rule of 4735.16(A) specifically, while C(13) is the broader duty to oversee the brokerage's overall compliance with advertising requirements generally
choice_b: They are identical, duplicate provisions with no meaningful difference
choice_c: C(2) applies only to branch offices while C(13) applies only to the brokerage's main office
choice_d: C(13) was repealed and fully replaced by C(2)
explanation: The two provisions are separately enumerated and serve different scopes: C(2) is a narrow cross-reference to specific office and advertising-disclosure rules, while C(13) is the general, standalone advertising-compliance-oversight duty.

topic: Broker Supervision, Principal Brokers & Management-Level Licensees
question: Under ORC 4735.081(C)(10), a principal broker must develop a written brokerage policy on agency that is separately required by which Chapter 4735 section?
explanation: ORC 4735.081(C)(10) cross-references ORC 4735.56 as the source of the written brokerage agency-policy requirement, distinct from the general written company agency policy required directly by C(9).

topic: Broker Supervision, Principal Brokers & Management-Level Licensees
question: ORC 4735.081(C)(9) and ORC 4735.081(C)(10) both address a principal broker's agency-policy duties. What distinguishes them?
choice_a: C(9) requires developing and maintaining a written company policy on agency relationships generally, while C(10) requires a written brokerage policy on agency specifically as required by ORC 4735.56 -- two separately enumerated statutory duties
choice_b: C(9) applies only to buyer clients and C(10) applies only to seller clients
choice_c: C(9) is mandatory while C(10) is entirely optional
choice_d: C(10) supersedes and repeals C(9)
explanation: The statute enumerates C(9) and C(10) as two distinct duties: one a general written agency-relationship policy, the other a written brokerage agency policy tied specifically to the separate requirement in ORC 4735.56.

topic: Broker Supervision, Principal Brokers & Management-Level Licensees
question: A principal broker has drafted a general written agency-relationship policy for the office but has never checked whether it independently satisfies the specific requirements of ORC 4735.56. Has the principal broker necessarily fulfilled both ORC 4735.081(C)(9) and (C)(10)?
choice_a: Not necessarily -- (C)(9) and (C)(10) are separate enumerated duties, and a policy satisfying the general (C)(9) requirement must still independently meet the specific cross-referenced requirements of ORC 4735.56 under (C)(10)
choice_b: Yes -- satisfying (C)(9) automatically satisfies (C)(10) because they cover identical ground
choice_c: No -- because ORC 4735.081(C)(10) has never actually been enacted
choice_d: Yes -- because ORC 4735.56 applies only to salespersons, not principal brokers
explanation: Because C(9) and C(10) are drafted as two independent enumerated duties, compliance with one does not automatically establish compliance with the other; the C(10) policy must specifically meet ORC 4735.56's requirements.

topic: Broker Supervision, Principal Brokers & Management-Level Licensees
question: Under ORC 4735.081(F), what effect does the section's list of principal-broker duties have on whether an affiliated licensee is classified as an independent contractor or an employee?
choice_a: None -- the section expressly states that nothing in it is to be considered prima facie evidence of independent-contractor or employee status
choice_b: It creates a rebuttable presumption of employee status
choice_c: It creates a conclusive presumption of independent-contractor status
choice_d: It automatically converts every affiliated licensee to employee status once supervisory duties are assigned
explanation: ORC 4735.081(F) provides that nothing in the section is prima facie evidence of whether an affiliated licensee is an independent contractor or an employee of the brokerage -- the duty list is not itself proof of a classification.

topic: Broker Supervision, Principal Brokers & Management-Level Licensees
question: In a wage dispute, a salesperson argues that because the principal broker "oversees and directs the operations of the brokerage" under ORC 4735.081(C)(1), the salesperson must be an employee rather than an independent contractor. Does ORC 4735.081 support that argument?
choice_a: No -- ORC 4735.081(F) expressly provides that nothing in the section is prima facie evidence of independent-contractor or employee status
choice_b: Yes -- the oversight duty in C(1) is dispositive proof of an employment relationship
choice_c: Yes, but only for salespersons hired after 2001
choice_d: No, because ORC 4735.081 does not apply to salespersons at all
explanation: ORC 4735.081(F) forecloses exactly this argument: the section's statutory oversight duties, including C(1), cannot be treated as prima facie evidence of employee or independent-contractor status.

topic: Broker Supervision, Principal Brokers & Management-Level Licensees
question: How does ORC 4735.081(F)'s independent-contractor/employee disclaimer interact with ORC 4735.091, which allows a licensee to associate with a brokerage as either an employee or an independent contractor?
choice_a: They are complementary -- 4735.091 confirms Ohio permits either arrangement, while 4735.081(F) ensures that a principal broker's statutory oversight duties are not themselves treated as evidence tipping that classification one way or the other
choice_b: They directly conflict, and 4735.081(F) has been held to override 4735.091
choice_c: ORC 4735.091 was repealed when 4735.081(F) was enacted
choice_d: ORC 4735.081(F) applies only to brokerages that elected employee status under 4735.091
explanation: The two provisions work together: 4735.091 confirms the underlying either-or arrangement Ohio allows, and 4735.081(F) protects that flexibility by keeping the principal broker's statutory duties out of the classification analysis.

topic: Broker Supervision, Principal Brokers & Management-Level Licensees
question: Under ORC 4735.18(A)(38), what conduct by a licensee is an explicit ground for discipline in connection with a principal broker's or management level licensee's duties?
choice_a: Having acted as a broker without authority, or having impeded a principal broker's ability to perform the duties described in ORC 4735.081, or having impeded a management level licensee's ability to perform the licensee's duties
choice_b: Merely disagreeing with a principal broker's ordinary business decisions
choice_c: Requesting a copy of the brokerage's written agency policy
choice_d: Reporting a principal broker's suspected misconduct to the superintendent
explanation: ORC 4735.18(A)(38) makes it a disciplinary ground to act as a broker without authority or to impede a principal broker's or management level licensee's ability to perform their respective ORC 4735.081 duties.

topic: Broker Supervision, Principal Brokers & Management-Level Licensees
question: A salesperson at a brokerage deliberately withholds transaction files from the principal broker, preventing the principal broker from maintaining accurate trust and transaction records as required by ORC 4735.081(C)(8). Could this expose the salesperson to discipline under Ohio law?
choice_a: Yes -- ORC 4735.18(A)(38) makes it a disciplinary ground to impede a principal broker's ability to perform duties described in ORC 4735.081, which includes the C(8) recordkeeping duty
choice_b: No -- only the principal broker, never the salesperson, can ever be disciplined for recordkeeping failures
choice_c: No -- ORC 4735.18(A)(38) applies only to brokers, not to salespersons
choice_d: No -- withholding files is a purely civil matter, entirely outside Chapter 4735's disciplinary scope
explanation: ORC 4735.18(A)(38) reaches any licensee, including a salesperson, who impedes a principal broker's ability to perform a 4735.081 duty -- here, the C(8) trust-and-transaction-recordkeeping duty.

topic: Broker Supervision, Principal Brokers & Management-Level Licensees
question: An affiliated broker repeatedly refuses to follow directives from a management level licensee who has been properly assigned supervisory authority over that broker's office under OAC 1301:5-6-01. Could this conduct expose the affiliated broker to discipline?
choice_a: Yes -- ORC 4735.18(A)(38) also makes it a disciplinary ground to impede a management level licensee's ability to perform the licensee's duties, not only a principal broker's
choice_b: No -- ORC 4735.18(A)(38) covers only interference with principal brokers, not management level licensees
choice_c: No -- a management level licensee has no authority a broker is ever obligated to follow
choice_d: No -- this conduct falls entirely outside Chapter 4735's scope
explanation: ORC 4735.18(A)(38) expressly extends to impeding a management level licensee's ability to perform the licensee's duties, mirroring the protection it gives principal brokers.

topic: Broker Supervision, Principal Brokers & Management-Level Licensees
question: Which Chapter 4735 provision supplies the disciplinary consequence for a licensee who impedes a principal broker's or management level licensee's ability to perform their ORC 4735.081 duties?
choice_a: ORC 4735.18(A)(38) -- grounds for discipline
choice_b: ORC 4735.081(F) -- the independent-contractor/employee disclaimer
choice_c: ORC 4735.12 -- the Real Estate Recovery Fund
choice_d: ORC 4735.24 -- trust account handling
explanation: ORC 4735.18(A) is Chapter 4735's central grounds-for-discipline provision, and its subsection (38) is the specific paragraph reaching interference with a principal broker's or management level licensee's 4735.081 duties.

topic: Broker Supervision, Principal Brokers & Management-Level Licensees
question: Broker Grant is designated principal broker of Brokerage X. The superintendent also approves Grant, under ORC 4735.081(E), to act as principal broker of Brokerage Y at the same time. Does Grant's designation at Brokerage Y relieve Grant of the ORC 4735.081(C) duties owed to Brokerage X?
choice_a: No -- serving as principal broker of Brokerage Y under the superintendent's (E) permission does not relieve Grant of the full set of C(1)-(14) duties owed separately to Brokerage X
choice_b: Yes -- Grant's duties are automatically split 50/50 between the two brokerages
choice_c: Yes -- Grant's duties to Brokerage X are suspended while acting for Brokerage Y
choice_d: No dual arrangement of this kind can ever be approved by the superintendent
explanation: ORC 4735.081(E) permits a broker to serve as principal broker of more than one brokerage, but it does not reduce or divide the C(1)-(14) duty set owed independently to each brokerage where the broker holds that designation.

topic: Broker Supervision, Principal Brokers & Management-Level Licensees
question: Which subsection of ORC 4735.081 gives the superintendent discretion to permit a broker to serve as principal broker of more than one brokerage, and is that permission automatic or discretionary?
choice_a: Subsection (E); the statute uses "may permit," making the arrangement discretionary with the superintendent rather than automatic
choice_b: Subsection (A); it is automatic for any broker with 5 or more years of licensed experience
choice_c: Subsection (C)(14); it becomes automatic once reported within 15 days
choice_d: Subsection (D); it requires no superintendent involvement at all
explanation: ORC 4735.081(E) uses permissive "may permit" language, placing multi-brokerage principal-broker arrangements within the superintendent's discretion rather than granting them automatically.

topic: Broker Supervision, Principal Brokers & Management-Level Licensees
question: A management level licensee at a branch office is asked by an affiliated salesperson whether the licensee's assigned oversight makes the licensee personally liable in place of the principal broker for the branch's overall statutory compliance. Under OAC 1301:5-6-01(C), what is the correct answer?
choice_a: The principal broker remains responsible to actively oversee and direct the brokerage's operations even after assigning supervisory duties to a management level licensee -- the assignment does not shift ultimate responsibility away from the principal broker
choice_b: Yes -- once duties are assigned, the management level licensee alone bears statutory responsibility
choice_c: Responsibility is shared exactly 50/50 between the principal broker and the management level licensee by rule
choice_d: Neither bears responsibility, because OAC 1301:5-6-01(C) was repealed
explanation: OAC 1301:5-6-01(C) states directly that assigning supervisory duties to a management level licensee does not diminish the principal broker's obligation to actively monitor and direct the brokerage's operations.

topic: Broker Supervision, Principal Brokers & Management-Level Licensees
question: A brokerage's principal broker dies unexpectedly and the brokerage has no other licensed broker on staff to immediately redesignate. Once a new principal broker is designated, which ORC 4735.081(B) duty is most immediately implicated?
choice_a: The 15-day requirement to report the change in principal broker designation to the superintendent
choice_b: A requirement to immediately dissolve the brokerage
choice_c: A requirement to refund all client trust funds within 24 hours
choice_d: A requirement to transfer the brokerage's license to the Ohio Real Estate Commission
explanation: Once a new principal broker is designated following the prior principal broker's death, ORC 4735.081(B)'s 15-day reporting obligation to the superintendent is triggered; the statute does not require dissolution, an immediate trust-fund refund, or a license transfer.

topic: Broker Supervision, Principal Brokers & Management-Level Licensees
question: A newly licensed broker joins a brokerage and is immediately assigned oversight of a two-person branch office, including supervising a salesperson whose buyer-agency duties sometimes conflict with another affiliated licensee's seller-agency duties. Has this broker met the OAC 1301:5-6-01(A) test for management level licensee status, even without ever being designated principal broker?
choice_a: Yes -- both conjunctive conditions are met: assigned oversight of a branch office, and supervision of licensees whose conflicting agency duties to clients require oversight
choice_b: No -- only a principal broker can ever qualify as a management level licensee
choice_c: No -- management level licensee status requires at least 5 years of licensure as a broker
choice_d: No -- the office must have at least 5 affiliated licensees to qualify
explanation: OAC 1301:5-6-01(A)'s two-part test does not require principal-broker status or a minimum tenure or office size -- it requires assigned oversight of an office/branch/division plus supervision involving potentially conflicting agency duties, both of which are met here.

topic: Broker Supervision, Principal Brokers & Management-Level Licensees
question: Does ORC 4735.081 permit a brokerage to operate with zero designated principal brokers, so long as the brokerage employs at least one management level licensee?
choice_a: No -- ORC 4735.081(A) requires every brokerage to designate at least one affiliated broker as principal broker; a management level licensee does not substitute for that designation
choice_b: Yes -- a sufficiently senior management level licensee can serve in lieu of a principal broker
choice_c: Yes, but only for brokerages with a single branch office
choice_d: Yes, provided the superintendent grants a hardship waiver under subsection (E)
explanation: ORC 4735.081(A)'s designation requirement is mandatory and brokerage-wide; a management level licensee, who need not even be a broker, cannot substitute for the required principal-broker designation.

topic: Broker Supervision, Principal Brokers & Management-Level Licensees
question: A brokerage's principal broker takes an extended two-month medical leave. During that time, no report is filed because the brokerage considers the leave temporary and does not designate a replacement. Does ORC 4735.081(B)'s 15-day reporting clock start merely because the principal broker is temporarily unavailable?
choice_a: No -- the 15-day clock in ORC 4735.081(B) runs from an actual change in the principal broker designation, not from a principal broker's temporary unavailability absent a redesignation
choice_b: Yes -- any absence longer than 30 days automatically triggers the reporting requirement
choice_c: Yes -- the clock starts on day one of any leave of absence, regardless of duration
choice_d: No -- the reporting requirement is triggered only by the principal broker's death, never by leave
explanation: ORC 4735.081(B) ties the 15-day clock to an actual change in designation; a temporary leave without a new designation does not, by itself, start that clock.

topic: Broker Supervision, Principal Brokers & Management-Level Licensees
question: OAC rule 1301:5-6-01 addresses management level licensees. What does the very next rule in that series, OAC 1301:5-6-02, address instead?
choice_a: When a licensee acting as host at an open house is considered an agent of the seller, and referral-fee disclosure rules -- a different subject from management-level-licensee supervision
choice_b: Additional principal-broker recordkeeping duties beyond those in ORC 4735.081(C)
choice_c: The Real Estate Recovery Fund claims process
choice_d: Continuing-education requirements specific to management level licensees
explanation: OAC 1301:5-6-02 governs open-house agency status and referral-fee disclosure, a distinct subject from OAC 1301:5-6-01's management-level-licensee supervisory framework, even though both rules sit in the same numbered series.

topic: Broker Supervision, Principal Brokers & Management-Level Licensees
question: A principal broker's written company policy on agency relationships under ORC 4735.081(C)(9) has not been updated in eight years, but the brokerage still displays the fair housing statement as required by C(3) and pays affiliated licensees promptly under C(11). Has the principal broker fully complied with ORC 4735.081(C) overall?
choice_a: Not necessarily -- ORC 4735.081(C) enumerates multiple separate duties, and compliance with some of them (C(3), C(11)) does not establish compliance with others, such as C(9)'s duty to develop and maintain a current written agency policy
choice_b: Yes -- complying with any three of the fourteen listed duties satisfies the section as a whole
choice_c: Yes -- C(9) only requires that the policy exist once, with no ongoing maintenance obligation
choice_d: No -- none of the fourteen listed duties have been satisfied because C(9) failed
explanation: ORC 4735.081(C) is a checklist of independently enforceable duties; satisfying some duties does not substitute for, or excuse, an ongoing failure under a different enumerated duty like C(9)'s maintain requirement.
